sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 46.6% a year from $6.91 billion in FY2017 to $215.9 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F211].
The shape is two step changes around a flat middle: revenue grew 125.9% in FY2024 and 114.2% in FY2025, after moving just 0.2% in FY2023 [D338][D393][D284].
The FY2024 jump came from Data Center revenue up 217%, driven by Hopper GPU shipments for LLM training and inference [P22][P23].
FY2026 growth of 65.5% was driven by Blackwell data center compute and networking platforms, with Data Center networking up 142% [D448][P8][P10].
Data Center was 89.7% of FY2026 revenue and contributed 60.2pp of the 65.5% growth [D620][D622][D448].
Within it, Compute contributed 46.1pp and Networking 14.1pp in FY2026, with Networking growing 141.5% [D629][D636][D635].
The filing attributes the increase to demand for the Blackwell computing platform and the ramp of NVLink compute fabric for GB200 and GB300 systems [P8].
Operating income grew 60.1% against revenue growth of 65.5%, an incremental operating margin of 57.3% [D449][D448][D475].
Operating costs grew 24.8pp slower than revenue, at 40.7% [D476][D468].
Operating margin of 60.4% in FY2026 sits above the 32.8% window median but below the 62.4% FY2025 high [F50][D813][D812].
Gross margin fell 3.9pp to 71.1%, driven by cost of revenue up 91.4% against revenue growth of 65.5% [D462][F30][D465][D448].
Compute & Networking operating income growth was partly offset by a $4.5 billion H20 excess inventory and purchase obligation charge in the first quarter of FY2026 [P7].
In FY2026 net margin of 55.6% sat 4.8pp below the 60.4% operating margin, as the 15.1% effective tax rate and other income pulled the two apart [F70][F50][D861][D434].
Operating cash flow of $102.7 billion was 0.86x net income, below the 0.97x window median [F100][D435][D851].
Free cash flow of $96.7 billion was a 44.8% margin, above the 44.4% window median [F110][D432][D822].
Capex of $6.04 billion was 2.8% of revenue and 2.13x D&A, the highest ratio in the five-year window [F105][D431][D437].
Cash used in investing rose to $52.2 billion, primarily on higher equity investment purchases and a non-exclusive license agreement with Groq [F120][P1].
Net cash was $34.7 billion at FY2025, 26.6% of revenue, against total debt of $8.47 billion [D386][D387][D440].
The FY2026 net-cash figure is not comparable because short-term investments were not reported that year, so the pack omits them [R3].
Return on average equity of 101.5% ranks at the 100th percentile of six semis peers against a 20.3% median [D447][D848][D849].
Buybacks and dividends of $41.1 billion absorbed 42.5% of free cash flow, and the diluted share count fell 1.2% [D443][D444][D470].
Short-term investments were not reported in FY2026 though reported in FY2025, so net cash and cash and investments for that year omit them [R3][X188].
This data gap means the FY2026 liquidity comparison and net-cash peer rank should not be relied on until the balance sheet is restated.
Graphics was 44.1% of revenue in FY2023 and fell 25.0% that year [R1][D753][D754].
That decline was a one-period cyclical drawdown, and Graphics has since recovered to 57.0% growth in FY2026, so it is not a persistent concern [D747].
Whether gross margin holds above the 71.1% FY2026 level or falls toward the 56.9% FY2023 low, reported in the FY2027 10-K [F30][D817].
Whether operating cash flow to net income recovers above the 0.97x window median from 0.86x in FY2026 [D435][D851].
Whether capex to D&A stays above 2.13x or falls back toward the 0.71x FY2024 level [D437][D327].
